findings.claim: The --source check says a path must be 'tracked' and is refused otherwise, 'since review due would report it as unresolved anyway'. That premise holds only in one case. review due tracks with `git ls-files` and skips every source outside git or in a shallow clone (with a note), and a file the agent wrote this session but has not yet added is untracked now but resolves after the commit. Read literally, the check refuses every --source outside git, and refuses the main case the new duty line is for: a concept written in the same change as the new code it describes. The check also has to resolve paths the way review_due._resolve does (concept folder first, then bundle, then repo root; a leading / means bundle-relative; .md appended), or it accepts paths review due cannot resolve and refuses ones it can. The plan needs to say what 'tracked' means: on disk, or in the git index, and what happens with no git or a shallow clone. It should also say the check reuses _resolve.

The plan gives --source to all five verbs, handoff included, and promises the concept comes due when its source changes. review_due skips handoffs before it reads sources (src/kmctl/review_due.py:161-166, the `continue`), so a handoff's sources are written but nothing reads them, and the help would promise something false for that verb. Also, the --key update path rebuilds a handoff's front matter from scratch (_front_matter in concepts.py), so it drops whatever an earlier call wrote. The plan should either refuse --source on handoff, as --key is refused on other kinds, or say it is recorded only and no reason fires for it.
